EDUTRACK
Plan it. Teach it. Grow from it.

The PLAN board — a whole year of lessons, one drag away.
01 — The Ask
Planning, teaching & accountability
live in three different places.
A classroom teacher plans a whole school year in a paper planbook, tracks standards in a district spreadsheet, and runs each day from memory or a sticky note. Nothing connects the plan to what actually gets taught — or to whether the standards were ever covered.
The brief: design a single, humane tool that ties long-range planning, the daily teaching hour, and standards coverage together — and makes planning a year feel approachable instead of paralyzing.
THE PAIN POINTS
Planning and standards tracking live in separate tools that never talk to each other.
A blank year is intimidating — long-range planning gets avoided.
Reflection is the first thing dropped when the week gets busy.
At report-card time, “did I actually cover this standard?” is a guess.
02 — The Solution
One planner, built on a loop
teachers already trust.
Everything lives inside a single rhythm — Plan → Do → Review — so the plan becomes the teaching day, and the teaching day becomes the record.
PLAN
The year, at a glance
A drag-and-drop board. A shelf of ready-to-teach, standards-aligned lessons plus short “Vitamins” — 10–15 minute boosters. Drag cards onto school days; unit bars, START/DUE flags, and a warning when a day runs past the block.
DO
The teaching hour
The plan becomes a daily run-of-show: an auto-timed agenda, expandable lesson plans with phase-by-phase timing, a materials checklist, and Confer & Capture — tap a student to log a note mid-lesson.
REVIEW
Coverage & reflection
Standards coverage rolls up automatically from what was planned and taught — taught / planned / not-yet, against a target. Plus a reflective lesson log with “Went well / Reteach” tags.
03 — Walkthrough
Inside the product.
THE PLANNING BOARD
Lessons look and behave like physical index cards you pick up and place onto weekdays. A colored unit bar runs beneath the timeline, arrows page through the year, and an orange badge appears the moment a day runs past the 105-minute block.
THE YEAR AT A GLANCE
Zoom out to the full marking period. A month strip charts the arc of the whole year — Character Study through Reflect & Celebrate — so a teacher can see pacing and gaps at a distance, then dive back into any week.
THE TEACHING DAY
DO turns the plan into a live run-of-show with real clock times. Each lesson expands into a phased plan; a side rail carries the day's materials, standards, and a lightweight way to capture conference notes on individual readers as you circulate.
COMPETENCY TRACKING
A standards grid fills itself in from what's on the board — a taught / planned / not-yet swatch for every standard, against a target. No double entry. Beside it, a lesson log invites a one-tap verdict and a sentence of reflection while it's fresh.
ONBOARDING & GUIDED TOUR
A one-minute setup gathers the classroom profile and loads a proven curriculum, then a spotlight tour walks the real interface — highlighting the lesson shelf, vitamins, and timeline in place. It's replayable anytime from the header.
04 — Craft
What made it feel real.
Bespoke drag & drop
Pointer-driven cards with a floating ghost, live drop targets, reordering, and real-time overload detection — no library.
Coverage from state
Standards tracking is computed from the board, not typed in by hand — the report writes itself as you plan.
Spotlight tour
An onboarding tour that tracks live DOM positions of real elements and re-anchors on window resize.
Nothing is lost
Every card, flag, note, and rating persists locally — the board is exactly where you left it, every morning.
05 — Design System
A planbook, not a dashboard.
Warm paper tones, a condensed almanac headline face, and physical cards you can pick up. Deliberately the opposite of sterile edtech.

06 — Why It Works
The value — a designer's take.
“The strongest idea in EduTrack isn't a feature — it's that accountability falls out of planning for free.”
It closes the loop.
Most tools do one of plan, teach, or assess. EduTrack's edge is that the three feed each other — the plan becomes the teaching day, the teaching day becomes the coverage record. That continuity is the whole product.
Compliance becomes a byproduct.
Standards tracking is usually a dreaded, separate chore. Here it's a passive benefit of work teachers already do. Turning an obligation into a free side-effect is a genuinely strong product move.
It lowers the activation cost.
Ready-made lessons, notes from teachers who taught them before, and a one-minute setup mean value on day one — not a blank canvas and a Sunday-night dread.
“Vitamins” are quietly brilliant.
Naming the small joyful moments — word games, fluency play — normalizes them and, crucially, makes them plannable. It's a design gesture that protects the humanity of a classroom.
Emotional design is the moat.
Warmth and tactility build attachment, and teachers protect tools they love. That's retention competitors can't clone with a feature list — and the wedge is a single teacher who adopts it, then pulls in the grade team.
Where it could grow.
Honestly: multi-class / multi-prep support, co-teacher collaboration, district curriculum import, and turning those captured conference notes into student-level insight over a whole year.
BOTTOM LINE
For teachers, EduTrack gives back hours and lowers anxiety. For schools, it quietly improves standards coverage and eases burnout. It earns its place not by adding features, but by connecting three things teachers were already doing — and making the connection feel good.
